title: Weekly Train to Link Nepal's Janakpur Dham With Ayodhya Over 604 Kilometres
excerpt: The government has announced a weekly service between Janakpur Dham and Ayodhya Cantt, departing Janakpur on Saturdays and Ayodhya on Mondays, with stops across Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
body:
• The government announced on Saturday a new weekly train service between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya Cantt in Uttar Pradesh.
  • The route covers approximately 604 kilometres, with commercial stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham.
  • Trains will originate from Janakpur Dham on Saturdays and from Ayodhya Cantt on Mondays, once a week in each direction.
  • For pilgrims, the service directly connects Janakpur, revered as the birthplace of Sita, with Ayodhya, the birthplace of Ram — the two anchor sites of the Ramayana tradition.

A weekly train will connect Janakpur Dham in Nepal with Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh, the government announced on Saturday, creating a direct rail link between the two cities at the heart of the Ramayana tradition.

Janakpur Dham is revered as the birthplace of Mata Sita and Ayodhya as the birthplace of Prabhu Shri Ram. According to the announcement reported by BizzBuzz, the service will cover approximately 604 kilometres between Janakpur Dham and Ayodhya Cantt, passing through towns and cities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

Route and schedule

Besides its terminal stations, the train will have commercial stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham. It will operate once a week, originating from Janakpur Dham on Saturdays and from Ayodhya Cantt on Mondays, Daily Kiran reported.

The announcement follows weeks of preparation on the corridor. Nepal railway officials said earlier this month that operating procedures and modalities were being negotiated between the two sides and were expected to be finalised within weeks, and that Indian Railways would operate the train initially, including setting facilities and fares, until Nepal is in a position to take over. A 17-coach Indian train made a trial run from Jaynagar to Kurtha earlier this month as part of those preparations.

"Route and schedule Besides its terminal stations, the train will have commercial stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham."

Why the link matters

Indian Railways said the initiative will give passengers from both countries improved access to the two religious and cultural centres and reinforce their shared civilisational heritage. For pilgrims, the practical effect is a single cross-border journey between the Ram Janmabhoomi temple city and Janakpur's Janaki Mandir, instead of a break of journey at the border.

The route also serves intermediate towns — Sitamarhi, Raxaul and Gorakhpur among them — giving travellers in north Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh a direct train toward both pilgrimage centres.

What travellers should watch for

The announcement sets the route, the stoppages and the operating days. It does not yet publish a start date, departure times, coach composition or fares; Nepal officials had earlier said fares and facilities would be decided by Indian Railways for the initial operation. Travellers planning a trip should wait for the formal timetable and booking opening before building an itinerary around the Saturday and Monday departures.
